chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Saif ibn Amira from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami from al-Mu'alla said:
"Take the wealth of the Naṣibī (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) wherever you find it, and send us the khums."
Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari said:

One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second) peace be upon him: "Inform me regarding the khums: is it upon all that a man acquires, from little and much, from all types, and upon the craftsmen, and how is that?" So he wrote with his own hand: "The khums is after expenses."

key_terms.اَلنَّاصِبِ: Naṣibī, one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.اَلْمَئُونَةِ: Al-ma'unah, expenses or living costs deducted before khums

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for paying khums on net income after expenses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic distinction between the specific confiscation of wealth from the *Naṣibī* (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt) and the general obligation of khums on net surplus income (*ba'da al-ma'unah*) for all believers. It underscores the practical application of khums across diverse professions, reflecting the Shia legal tradition's emphasis on financial purification after deducting living expenses.
